sources.title: Experimental Validation of User Experience-focused Dynamic Onboard Service Orchestration for Software Defined Vehicles
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The paper evaluates the previously proposed dynamic onboard service-orchestration algorithm on a dedicated test bench to assess practical onboard feasibility.

The orchestration algorithm uses real-time in-vehicle/V2X network health and onboard resource constraints to choose degraded application modes while balancing user experience and mixed-criticality QoS requirements.
claims.context: Architecture/algorithm carried from the authors' prior work.

claims.text: AXIL is used as a runtime priority notion for non-safety-critical applications in the orchestration scheme.

limitations.text: The primary abstract states that a dedicated test bench was used but does not expose its hardware/network composition, workload, baselines, measured execution times, or QoS outcomes.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Experimental Validation of User Experience-focused Dynamic Onboard Service Orchestration for Software Defined Vehicles; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary page verifies that dedicated test-bench validation was performed and confirms the orchestration/AXIL scope, but detailed experiment conditions and results require full-paper inspection.

editorial.why_now_note: Dynamic service placement/degradation turns onboard resource governance into a runtime architectural function, making the test-bench follow-up materially relevant.
editorial.rationale: This is the empirical follow-up to the orchestration concept and likely stronger than the simulation-only precursor, but the accessible primary abstract does not expose the test-bench configuration or numerical results.
